analysis: Exact partitions of 25 slices coincide with symbol-count partitions; completion of the swap relations is the finite system {yx -> xy | x < y} whose normal forms are sorted words.
assumptions: words of bounded length (exact, since the relations preserve length)
falsification: Any slice where a class contains two words with different projections, or two words with equal projections lie in different classes, or completion fails/normal form differs.

history.new: Exact partitions of 25 slices coincide with symbol-count partitions; completion of the swap relations is the finite system {yx -> xy | x < y} whose normal forms are sorted words.

hypothesis: Two words are congruent iff, for every symbol s, deleting all other symbols gives the same word s...s (equal symbol projections). The shortlex-completed system {yx -> xy : x < y} is finite and its normal forms are the sorted words.
methodology: For every alphabet/length slice, compute the exact congruence classes by union-find over single swap steps; compare the partition with the projection partition; run shortlex Knuth-Bendix completion and compare normal forms with sorted words.
question: In System A with the swap relations xy <-> yx, what distinguishes two words that cannot be transformed into each other?

summary: 25 alphabet/length slices checked exactly (up to 4235 words in the largest slices); all checks passed: True
